outcome: LifeMax exposes an unauthenticated GET /api/health route that returns HTTP 200 with a small JSON body ({ status: "ok", uptimeSeconds, version }) when the process is up and the database is reachable, and HTTP 503 with { status: "degraded", reason } when the database check fails. No owner data, secrets, or setup state are exposed.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/health returns 200 and JSON { status: "ok", uptimeSeconds: <number>, version: <string> } on a healthy process
When the database health probe throws, the route returns 503 and JSON { status: "degraded", reason: <short string> } without leaking a stack trace
The route requires no authentication and is reachable with SETUP_MODE=disabled
Response contains no owner PII, password state, environment values, or setup tokens
An automated test (unit or integration, matching the repo's existing test style) covers the 200 and 503 paths
constraints: Next.js App Router route under src/app/api/health/route.ts; follow the patterns already in src/app/api and src/infrastructure/db
Reuse the existing DB accessor / clock abstractions in src/infrastructure — do not open a raw connection
Do not change auth, setup, or migration code
Keep the payload minimal and non-sensitive; no per-request logging of the body
